evidence.detail:
Medium confirmed with Nick. Related acid / calcium technology; system claims and brand advice do not prove equivalent effects with arbitrary partner products.

Citric-acid research supports plausibility. Whole-line claims are not read as an isolated effect of this concentrate.

A named US Kérastase education manager recommends weekly use. Commercially affiliated professional advice, not independent efficacy testing.

Restorative calcium / damage treatment; no intensity ranking.

Historical v0.3 evidence observations (owner grades and selected Redken source now follow the later owner decision):

Headline restoration/routine results remain multi-product outcomes; no isolated numerical treatment effect can be assigned.

E01/N07 report acid-treated chemically damaged fibres, not the retail bottle. Full dose, pH, vehicle, duration, n and statistics are inaccessible.

The earlier shampoo-style manufacturer capture remains displaced with an explicit mismatch reason; it is not treated as the treatment formula or silently erased. The 45 ml capture is contextual, not proof of 250 ml identity.

E01/N07 are the same L’Oréal Research & Innovation paper, declared no conflict; report damage-dependent endpoints and do not represent independent convergence.

N01/N02 are retailer identity/protocol corroboration, not clinical validation or a physical pack check.

An acid treatment followed directly by the required shampoo is a multi-step use; retain that exact requirement and do not substitute an unrelated rinse-off protocol.

No system percentage, abstract effect percentage, active concentration, all-hair suitability or efficacy rank is transferred.

Research admission is source-version candidacy only; fit, protocol compatibility, catalog binding and publication remain separate.
